story.heading: Coaching built for the life you actually live.
story.lead:
I'm Pratyush, and I have gone through a fitness transformation myself. 
With the rising awareness around fitness, there's also rising misinformation, which keeps most people stuck. 
You probably think there's IMMENSE sacrifice involved. It's not, you just need a plan that fits YOUR routine.
My goal is to help you lose fat and build muscle without putting your career, travel or family time on hold.
story.p1: Most plans are written for people with 4 spare hours a day. You don't have that with early meetings, deadlines, client dinners, flights and families. So the plan has to be built around the week you actually have, not the one a template assumes.
story.p2: That's the goal: Building a system that fits your life, so you can get the results without overthinking.
story.p3:
Personalised training around your schedule and equipment. 
Flexible nutrition that survives travel and eating out. Weekly check-ins, form reviews and direct access, so small problems get fixed before they turn into plateaus, and so you actually understand the deeper concepts, not just follow orders.
story.pull: Your schedule isn't an obstacle. It's the thing we build the plan around.
story.p4: Every client works with me for 3, 6 or 12 months and finishes with the habits, mindset and a maintenance plan to keep the results for good. My job isn't to hand you a 12-week fix, it's to make sure you never need one again.

faqs.q: How much time does this actually take?
faqs.a: Most clients train 3-5 hours per week, plus about ten minutes a day for tracking. The program is built around your real availability in week one. If your schedule changes, the plan changes with it.

faqs.q: Do I need a gym, or specific equipment?
faqs.a: No. Programs are written for whatever you have: a full commercial gym, a home setup, or hotel gyms while travelling. The system adapts to the tools, not the reverse.

faqs.q: I travel and eat out a lot. Will this survive that?
faqs.a: It's designed for exactly that. Your nutrition runs on flexible targets and real-world strategies rather than rigid meal plans, and travel, holidays and client dinners are planned for in advance, not punished.

faqs.q: What happens in a weekly check-in?
faqs.a: You submit your data, photos and any form videos; Pratyush reviews everything, records a response covering what's working and what changes next week, and you talk through anything that needs a decision on a call or voice note.

faqs.q: How soon will I see results?
faqs.a: Most clients see measurable change on the scale and tape within three to four weeks, and visible change in photos by weeks six to eight. The honest answer: speed depends on your consistency, and consistency is exactly what the system is built to protect.

faqs.q: How long do I sign up for?
faqs.a: Coaching runs in 3, 6 or 12-month commitments. Longer isn't upselling, it's how lasting change actually happens. Every client finishes with a maintenance plan so the results hold once coaching ends.

posts.title: 5 Simple Habits That Actually Move the Needle
posts.excerpt: Flexible targets, not banned lists. The exact framework busy professionals use to hit their goals without skipping client dinners
posts.body:
5 Simple Habits That Actually Move the Needle

Move every day, even briefly. A 10-minute walk counts more than a missed hour-long workout.

Prioritize protein at breakfast. It curbs cravings and keeps energy steady.

Track one number. Whether it's steps, reps, or sleep — pick one metric and watch it improve.

Sleep like it's part of training. Recovery is where the real gains happen.

Celebrate small wins. Consistency is built on momentum, not perfection.

posts.title: The 10-Minute Rule
posts.excerpt: A minimalist split built for hotel gyms and unpredictable weeks, so momentum survives your calendar.
posts.body: Some days you don't have an hour. You barely have ten minutes. Here's the secret: take it anyway. Commit to just 10 minutes of movement — a walk, some bodyweight squats, a few sets of push-ups. More often than not, once you start, you'll keep going. And on the days you don't? Ten minutes still beats zero. Consistency isn't built on perfect days. It's built on showing up imperfectly, over and over.

posts.title: Rest Days Aren't Lazy Days
posts.excerpt: The uncomfortable truth about transformation: the boring, repeatable stuff is what actually changes your body.
posts.body: Muscles don't grow in the gym they grow during recovery. Skipping rest days in the name of "hustle" often backfires: fatigue builds, form breaks down, and injury risk climbs. A true rest day (or an active recovery day with light walking or stretching) is part of the training, not a break from it. Respect the rest, and your next workout will be stronger for it.

posts.title: The Habit That Changes Everything: Tracking Your Water Intake
posts.body: It sounds too simple to matter, but hydration affects energy, focus, digestion, and workout performance. Most people underestimate how much water they actually need — especially if they're active. Try carrying a bottle and refilling it a set number of times a day rather than guessing. Small habit, big payoff.
